messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>

Subject: Dedicated capacity: sizing runway & validation next steps

Thanks again for the call this morning, Emma — solid conversation and appreciate the clear traffic numbers you shared. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on performance gating for a Dedicated deployment.

Key goals you mentioned:
- 95th pct tail latency target: <= 150ms (short prompts, baseline 256 tokens)
- Streaming support (token-by-token progress) for long-form generation
- Concurrent active sessions: expected 450–600 users during peak 10–11am PT window; bursts up to ~1k for events
- SLO: 99.9% availability for inference endpoints during business hours

Immediate asks we agreed to:
1) You to share a representative traffic profile CSV (request/seq_len distribution) — you said you would export yesterday evening.
2) We’ll run a focused Dedicated sizing proposal (GPU candidate comparison + reserved throughput) and propose a 1-week validation plan to gate SLOs.
3) Schedule a 90-min technical validation session with your infra + SRE folks next week for live perf tests.

Initial sizing notes (high level):
- For your concurrency/latency targets we’re likely looking at 2 rack-equivalent Dedicated pools: primary capacity sized for steady 600 concurrent sessions and a hot spare pool for burst absorb and failover.
- Candidate GPUs we’ll benchmark: A100 80GB (FP16), H100 80GB (bfloat/FP8 path), and L40s (cost-optimized FP16).
- Target reserved throughput: 120–150 req/s sustained (short prompts) with autoscaling policy to 300 req/s burst.

Attachments: I’ll attach the traffic profile you promised as soon as we have it and our preliminary sizing worksheet. For now I’m attaching the internal template we’ll use (sizing_calc.xlsx) and a short slide deck with GPU tradeoffs (gpu_compare_slides.pdf).

Next steps:
- Emma: confirm availability for a technical validation slot (Wed/Thu preferred) and confirm which SRE will join.
- We’ll prepare a runbook for the live validation (we’ll include perf scripts, data masks, and pass/fail criteria).

Thanks — I’ll follow up internally with bench configs and a proposed validation agenda.

—

Subject: Internal: StratoHealth — quick GPU candidate sizing & validation plan

Ben / Tessa — forwarding Emma’s profile (attached) and my notes from the call. I want a crisp recommendation by EOD so we can send a short proposal before tomorrow’s validation session. Highlights and asks: 

From the traffic profile:
- Peak sustained request rate (10–11am PT): ~130 req/s
- Concurrent active sessions: median 520, 95th ~820 (burst spikes)
- Short prompts dominant; long tail (2–3k tokens) at ~5% of sessions drives KV cache pressure

Sizing constraints and candidate comparison (rough rough):
- A100 80GB (FP16): best-established perf for KV-heavy sequences; expect ~1.2x throughput vs L40s for our model family; cost: high
- H100 80GB (FP8 path): best tail-latency for streaming with reduced latency at scale; good for low-99th but requires newer runtime path; higher unit cost, less time-tested in customer infra
- L40s: best cost/throughput trade for short prompts; lower memory headroom for long-context; economical for large reserved pools

Proposed starting config for the validation run:
- Primary pool: 4x A100 80GB nodes (reserved) — baseline to validate tail latency at 600 concurrent; set reserved throughput to 140 req/s with autoscale to 320 req/s
- Hot spare pool: 2x L40s nodes for burst/fallback behavior and cost testing
- If H100 shows meaningful tail improvement in our bench, swap one A100 for an H100 in week 2 of validation to compare 95/99th delta

Perf tests to include for the session:
- Short prompt ramp (1–150 tokens) for throughput and 95th latency
- Long streaming sessions (2–3k tokens) to validate streaming token latency and KV cache behavior
- Failover: shift 30% traffic to hot spare and observe latency impact

Attachments: I’ve updated sizing_calc.xlsx with numbers based on the csv and added a one-pager with bench knobs in gpu_compare_slides.pdf — please review.

Quick ask: Ben, can you prepare candidate bench scripts (1) short-serialized QPS test (2) streaming token-by-token test and share the execution commands by 16:00 PT? Tessa — add the runtime flags we need to exercise both FP16 and FP8 code paths and a checklist for measurables.

Thanks — will send the external note once we have your signoff.

—
Camila
